title: Stage 1 — Working commerce platform
note: PostgreSQL owns transactional truth. Derived stores are eventually consistent. Kubernetes and telemetry span all workloads. Analytics ends in Superset dashboards.

title: Domain boundaries and ownership
note: Logical services may share a local PostgreSQL host, but never each other’s private tables. Payments, Fulfillment and Reviews are additional bounded contexts.

title: Infrastructure and delivery bootstrap
note: Terraform provisions infrastructure; Helm deploys application workloads. Secrets stay outside Git. Migrations require a compatibility and rollback strategy.

title: Catalog, stock and synthetic fixtures
note: Seed relationships and constraints, not independent random rows. Prices, orders and stock must reconcile. Dataset reset must be deterministic.

title: Storefront, search and cart
note: Search price and availability may lag. Checkout revalidates authoritative price and inventory. Cache keys must respect relevant user scope.

title: Checkout Saga and compensation
note: Workflow records outcomes and updates Orders through its API. Capture timing is an explicit policy. Compensation is not rollback and may require manual resolution.

title: Outbox, Kafka and CQRS
note: Delivery can repeat. Enforce deduplication and document ordering scope. CQRS does not require event sourcing. Rebuild projections from retained events or an authoritative snapshot.

title: Post-purchase workflows
note: Refund and restock are independent business steps. Validate order ownership, return windows and duplicate requests. Cancellation and partial returns require explicit policies.

title: Graph, lakehouse and reporting
note: Iceberg also needs a catalog service selected during implementation. Reconcile financial totals to commerce. Add ClickHouse only for a justified low-latency analytical workload.

title: Reliability, scaling and recovery
note: Stateful failover is not solved by application replicas. Publish measured capacity, recovery objectives and actual restore results for the declared environment.

title: Stage 2 — Rufus requirements and design
note: Design stage only: candidate components are not implemented capabilities. Requirements trace back to working stage-1 services.

title: Journeys, permissions and autonomy
note: Define when to clarify, refuse, escalate or ask approval. Purchasing requires approval bound to the actual proposed action.

title: Knowledge, semantic layer and memory
note: Current prices and stock come from authoritative tools. Memory has retention, correction and deletion policies. Context selects what the model sees; it is not the memory store.

title: Bounded agent runtime and MCP tools
note: Tool results return to persisted graph state for the next bounded step. Stop on completion, budget exhaustion or escalation. MCP exposes tools; it does not replace authorization.

title: Quality, guardrails and caching design
note: Cache classes: response, retrieval, embedding, tool result, semantic and provider-supported prefix caches. Similar meaning alone is insufficient for a safe cache hit.

title: Design review and gap traceability
note: Exit gate: reviewed architecture, feasible local profile and measurable evaluation targets. No invented implementation status.

title: Stage 3 — Extend and integrate the assistant
note: Stage 3 implements stage-2 gaps. The agent does not access private service tables or directly own stock/payment transactions.

title: Safe commerce extensions
note: Extend provenance, structured errors, freshness and missing events according to the gap matrix. Maintain storefront and event backward compatibility.

title: Read-only shopping assistant
note: Evaluate qualifying recommendations, missing evidence, conflicting reviews, stale projections and injection attempts before enabling writes.

title: Approval and durable action execution
note: An expired or stale proposal cannot authorize a different purchase. Decline/expiry ends or revises the proposal; worker restart resumes from durable state.

title: Memory, context and cache correctness
note: Valid cached answers may bypass generation only under explicit policy. Never cache personalized or live transactional answers solely by semantic similarity.

title: Enterprise roles and specialist capabilities
note: Specialist workflows do not require separate agents. Add delegation only when it beats the simpler baseline and preserves role/tenant isolation.

title: Integrated quality and release gates
note: Measure p95 latency, successful task cost and recovery on declared hardware and data. Quality gates compare versioned datasets, not a hand-picked demo.
